entries.original: Cu mancia fa muddichi.
entries.literal_it: Chi mangia fa briciole.
entries.literal_en: Whoever eats makes crumbs.
entries.meaning_it: Chi agisce può sbagliare; ogni azione lascia tracce.
entries.meaning_en: Whoever does things makes mistakes.
entries.usage_context: Consolation after a bug or an error; defending someone who tried.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cu 'un fa nenti 'un sbaglia nenti.
entries.literal_it: Chi non fa niente non sbaglia niente.
entries.literal_en: Who does nothing gets nothing wrong.
entries.meaning_it: Solo chi non fa niente non sbaglia mai.
entries.meaning_en: Only those who do nothing never err.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cu nesci, arrinesci.
entries.literal_it: Chi esce, riesce.
entries.literal_en: Who goes out, succeeds.
entries.meaning_it: Chi esce dal proprio guscio (o parte) ha successo.
entries.meaning_en: Those who venture out succeed.
entries.usage_context: Encouraging someone to change job, learn something new, leave comfort zone.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cu' ha lingua passa 'u mari.
entries.literal_it: Chi ha lingua passa il mare.
entries.literal_en: Who has a tongue crosses the sea.
entries.meaning_it: Chi sa parlare e chiedere arriva lontano.
entries.meaning_en: Those who can speak up (and ask) go far.
entries.usage_context: Advice to ask questions, communicate, document.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Comu la 'mpastasti, scanatilla.
entries.literal_it: Come l'hai impastata, spianatela.
entries.literal_en: As you kneaded it, roll it out.
entries.meaning_it: Devi affrontare le conseguenze delle tue scelte.
entries.meaning_en: You made your bed, now lie in it.
entries.usage_context: Wrong choices, own architecture decisions, tech debt you created.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Càlati juncu ca passa la china.
entries.literal_it: Piegati giunco che passa la piena.
entries.literal_en: Bend, reed, the flood is passing.
entries.meaning_it: Nei momenti duri conviene piegarsi e aspettare che passino.
entries.meaning_en: Bend with the storm until it passes.
entries.usage_context: Bad days, crunch time, angry managers, incidents.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: L'arvulu s'addrizza mentri è virdi.
entries.literal_it: L'albero si raddrizza mentre è verde.
entries.literal_en: A tree is straightened while it is green.
entries.meaning_it: Le abitudini si correggono presto.
entries.meaning_en: Fix habits early.
entries.usage_context: Teaching juniors, linting early, code review from day one.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Un arvulu a primu corpu nun si tagghia.
entries.literal_it: Un albero non si abbatte al primo colpo.
entries.literal_en: A tree is not felled at the first blow.
entries.meaning_it: Le cose grandi richiedono tempo e pazienza.
entries.meaning_en: Big things take patience.
entries.usage_context: Why not to rush; long refactors; learning.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cosi longhi addiventanu serpi.
entries.literal_it: Le cose lunghe diventano serpi.
entries.literal_en: Long things turn into snakes.
entries.meaning_it: Le cose rimandate troppo si complicano.
entries.meaning_en: Things dragged on turn nasty.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cu' sputa 'n celu 'n facci cci torna.
variants: Cu' sputa all'aria 'n facci cci torna.
entries.literal_it: Chi sputa in cielo gli torna in faccia.
entries.literal_en: Who spits at the sky gets it back in the face.
entries.meaning_it: Chi offende o fa danni se li ritrova addosso.
entries.meaning_en: What goes around comes around.
entries.usage_context: Arrogant colleagues, karma for bad code.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cui scava lu fossu, lu primu ci cadi.
entries.literal_it: Chi scava il fosso ci cade per primo.
entries.literal_en: Who digs the pit falls in first.
entries.meaning_it: Chi prepara trappole agli altri ci cade.
entries.meaning_en: Those who set traps fall into them.
entries.usage_context: Colleague who sabotages; hacks that backfire.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Megghiu lu tintu conusciutu, ca lu bonu a conusciri.
entries.literal_it: Meglio il cattivo conosciuto che il buono da conoscere.
entries.literal_en: Better the bad you know than the good still to be known.
entries.meaning_it: Meglio ciò che si conosce, anche se imperfetto, dell'ignoto.
entries.meaning_en: Better the devil you know.
entries.usage_context: Choosing between a legacy stack and a shiny new framework.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Megghiu accordiu magru ca sintenzia grassa.
entries.literal_it: Meglio un accordo magro che una sentenza grassa.
entries.literal_en: Better a lean agreement than a fat verdict.
entries.meaning_it: Meglio un compromesso che una lite vinta a caro prezzo.
entries.meaning_en: A lean settlement beats a fat lawsuit.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Supra 'o vagnatu, cci chiovi.
entries.literal_it: Sul bagnato ci piove.
entries.literal_en: It rains on what is already wet.
entries.meaning_it: Le disgrazie colpiscono chi è già sfortunato.
entries.meaning_en: When it rains, it pours.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: A li poviri e a li sbinturati, ci chiovi 'nta lu culu macari assittati.
entries.literal_it: Ai poveri e agli sventurati piove nel sedere anche da seduti.
entries.literal_en: On the poor and unlucky it rains on their backside even when they are sitting.
entries.meaning_it: Ai sfortunati va male qualunque cosa facciano.
entries.meaning_en: Nothing goes right for the unlucky.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: A navi rutta ogni ventu è cuntrariu.
entries.literal_it: A nave rotta ogni vento è contrario.
entries.literal_en: To a broken ship every wind is against.
entries.meaning_it: Quando le cose vanno male tutto sembra contro.
entries.meaning_en: When things are broken, everything is against you.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Un pumu fradiciu nni guasta 'na cartedda.
entries.literal_it: Una mela fradicia ne guasta una cesta.
entries.literal_en: One rotten apple spoils a basket.
entries.meaning_it: Un elemento negativo rovina tutto il gruppo.
entries.meaning_en: One bad apple spoils the bunch.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Ci voli assai pi sapiri picca.
entries.literal_it: Ci vuole molto per sapere poco.
entries.literal_en: It takes a lot to know a little.
entries.meaning_it: Imparare costa fatica.
entries.meaning_en: Learning takes great effort.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: È megghiu sapiri picca, chi parrari assai.
entries.literal_it: È meglio sapere poco che parlare molto.
entries.literal_en: Better to know little than to talk a lot.
entries.meaning_it: Meglio tacere che parlare a vanvera.
entries.meaning_en: Better to know a little than to talk too much.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cu' pò nun vò, cu' vò nun pò, cu' fa nun sa, cu' sa nun fa, e 'cussì tuttu lu munnu va.
entries.literal_it: Chi può non vuole, chi vuole non può, chi fa non sa, chi sa non fa, e così va il mondo.
entries.literal_en: Who can won't, who will can't, who does doesn't know, who knows doesn't do: so the world goes.
entries.meaning_it: Il mondo va storto perché capacità e volontà non coincidono.
entries.meaning_en: That's how the world (and the company) works.
entries.usage_context: Ironic comment on organisations and projects.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Duru cu duru nun fabbrica muru.
entries.literal_it: Duro con duro non fabbrica muro.
entries.literal_en: Hard with hard builds no wall.
entries.meaning_it: Due testardi non concludono niente.
entries.meaning_en: Two stubborn people build nothing.
entries.usage_context: Conflict with a colleague, code review fights.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Quannu 'u diavulu t'accarizza, voli l'arma.
entries.literal_it: Quando il diavolo ti accarezza, vuole l'anima.
entries.literal_en: When the devil caresses you, he wants your soul.
entries.meaning_it: Diffida di chi ti lusinga troppo.
entries.meaning_en: Beware of flatterers.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: La gaddina fa l'ovu e lu gaddu grida.
entries.literal_it: La gallina fa l'uovo e il gallo grida.
entries.literal_en: The hen lays the egg and the rooster crows.
entries.meaning_it: Uno lavora e un altro se ne prende il merito.
entries.meaning_en: One does the work, another takes the credit.
entries.usage_context: Colleague who takes credit for your work.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: 'U sceccu 'a potta, 'u sceccu sa mangia.
variants: L'asinu porta la pagghia, e l'asinu si la mancia.
entries.literal_it: L'asino la porta, l'asino se la mangia.
entries.literal_en: The donkey carries it, the donkey eats it.
entries.meaning_it: Chi fatica è poi chi ne paga o ne gode le conseguenze.
entries.meaning_en: You carry it, you eat it.
entries.geographical_area: Sicilian, attested in a form with Catanese phonology
entries.notes: potta = Catanese r+C assimilation of porta.

entries.original: 'U voi ci dici curnutu 'o sceccu.
entries.literal_it: Il bue dice cornuto all'asino.
entries.literal_en: The ox calls the donkey a cuckold.
entries.meaning_it: Si critica negli altri un difetto che si ha.
entries.meaning_en: The pot calling the kettle black.
entries.usage_context: Colleague criticising code as messy as his own.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)
entries.notes: In Catanese pronunciation curnutu is often realised cunnutu.

entries.original: A vita iè comu a scala do puddaru... iè cutta e china 'i medda!
entries.literal_it: La vita è come la scala del pollaio: corta e piena di merda.
entries.literal_en: Life is like a henhouse ladder: short and full of shit.
entries.meaning_it: La vita è breve e piena di fastidi.
entries.meaning_en: Life is short and full of crap.
entries.geographical_area: Sicilian, attested in a form with Catanese phonology
entries.notes: cutta, medda show Catanese r+C assimilation (curta, merda).

entries.original: Quannu l'amicu nun parra a prima vuci, voddiri ca 'u riscussu nun ci piaci.
entries.literal_it: Quando l'amico non risponde subito, vuol dire che il discorso non gli piace.
entries.literal_en: When a friend doesn't answer at first call, the topic doesn't please him.
entries.meaning_it: Il silenzio è già una risposta.
entries.meaning_en: Silence is an answer.
entries.geographical_area: Sicilian, attested in a form with Catanese phonology
entries.notes: voddiri, riscussu show Catanese assimilation and d>r.

entries.original: Jurnata rutta perdila tutta.
entries.literal_it: Giornata interrotta, perdila tutta.
entries.literal_en: A broken day, lose it all.
entries.meaning_it: Una giornata compromessa è meglio lasciarla perdere.
entries.meaning_en: A ruined day is a lost day.
entries.usage_context: Bad day, call it a day.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Ogni fruttu voli la so staggiuni.
entries.literal_it: Ogni frutto vuole la sua stagione.
entries.literal_en: Every fruit wants its season.
entries.meaning_it: Ogni cosa ha i suoi tempi.
entries.meaning_en: Everything in its own time.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Truniannu truniannu chioviri voli.
entries.literal_it: Tuonando tuonando vuol piovere.
entries.literal_en: Thundering and thundering, it wants to rain.
entries.meaning_it: I segnali premonitori annunciano il guaio.
entries.meaning_en: Repeated warnings precede trouble.
entries.usage_context: Ignored warnings in logs, flaky tests.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Vutti chi nun è attuppata, sventa.
entries.literal_it: La botte non tappata sfiata.
entries.literal_en: A barrel not stoppered loses its gas.
entries.meaning_it: Ciò che non è chiuso bene si perde (anche segreti).
entries.meaning_en: What isn't sealed leaks.
entries.usage_context: Secrets in repos, security, open ports.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Chiddu chi si schifa, veni tempu chi s'addisia.
variants: Zoccu si schifìa veni tempu ca s'addisìa.
entries.literal_it: Ciò che si disprezza, verrà il tempo che si desidera.
entries.literal_en: What you scorn, the time will come when you crave it.
entries.meaning_it: Non disprezzare oggi ciò che domani ti servirà.
entries.meaning_en: Don't scorn what you may need later.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Ammatula ca t'allisci e fai cannola, 'u santu è di mammuru e nun sura.
entries.literal_it: È inutile che ti fai bella e prepari dolci, il santo è di marmo e non suda.
entries.literal_en: It's useless to primp and make cannoli: the saint is marble and doesn't sweat.
entries.meaning_it: È inutile insistere con chi non si lascia smuovere.
entries.meaning_en: No use trying to move the unmovable.
entries.usage_context: Trying to convince a stubborn manager or a broken tool.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)
entries.notes: Popularised by Franco Battiato (from Riposto, Catania area).

entries.original: Cunti senza l'osti si fanno dui voti.
entries.literal_it: I conti senza l'oste si fanno due volte.
entries.literal_en: Bills made without the innkeeper are made twice.
entries.meaning_it: Le stime fatte senza chi decide vanno rifatte.
entries.meaning_en: Plans made without the stakeholder get redone.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Testa chi nun parra si chiama cucuzza.
entries.literal_it: Testa che non parla si chiama zucca.
entries.literal_en: A head that doesn't speak is called a pumpkin.
entries.meaning_it: Chi non chiede e non si esprime resta ignorante.
entries.meaning_en: A head that never asks is a pumpkin.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cu' simina spini nun pò raccogghiri rosi.
variants: Cui simina spini, nun ricogghi rosi.
entries.literal_it: Chi semina spine non può raccogliere rose.
entries.literal_en: Who sows thorns can't reap roses.
entries.meaning_it: Chi fa male raccoglie male.
entries.meaning_en: You reap what you sow.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Bisogna masticari amaru, cui voli a tempu agghiuttiri duci.
entries.literal_it: Deve masticare amaro chi vuole a tempo debito inghiottire dolce.
entries.literal_en: Chew bitter now to swallow sweet later.
entries.meaning_it: Per ottenere risultati bisogna fare sacrifici.
entries.meaning_en: No pain, no gain.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cui sceccu fa cavaddu, lu primu cauci è so.
variants: Cu du sceccu, ni fa mulu u primu cauci è u so.
entries.literal_it: Chi fa di un asino un cavallo, il primo calcio è suo.
entries.literal_en: Whoever makes a horse of a donkey gets the first kick.
entries.meaning_it: Chi favorisce gli immeritevoli ne riceve ingratitudine.
entries.meaning_en: Promote a donkey and you get the first kick.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Cu paja prima, mancia li pisci fitùsi.
entries.literal_it: Chi paga prima mangia i pesci puzzolenti.
entries.literal_en: Who pays first eats the stinking fish.
entries.meaning_it: Chi paga prima di vedere la merce viene fregato.
entries.meaning_en: Pay up front and get cheated.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Munnu ha statu e munnu è.
entries.literal_it: Il mondo è stato ed è (sempre lo stesso).
entries.literal_en: The world has been and the world is.
entries.meaning_it: Le cose si ripetono, è difficile cambiarle.
entries.meaning_en: Nothing new under the sun.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Azzappa all'acqua e simina o ventu.
entries.literal_it: Zappa l'acqua e semina al vento.
entries.literal_en: He hoes water and sows in the wind.
entries.meaning_it: Fatica sprecata, risultato nullo.
entries.meaning_en: Wasted effort.
entries.usage_context: Useless work, writing code nobody uses.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: 'A megghiu parola è chidda ca nun si dici.
entries.literal_it: La parola migliore è quella che non si dice.
entries.literal_en: The best word is the one not said.
entries.meaning_it: A volte tacere è la scelta più saggia.
entries.meaning_en: Sometimes silence is wisest.
entries.usage_context: Heated chats, flame wars, angry emails.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Ogni figateddu 'i musca jè sustanza.
entries.literal_it: Ogni fegatino di mosca è sostanza.
entries.literal_en: Every fly's liver is nourishment.
entries.meaning_it: Anche il contributo più piccolo conta.
entries.meaning_en: Every little bit helps.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Nìuru cu nìuru non tingi.
entries.literal_it: Nero con nero non tinge.
entries.literal_en: Black on black doesn't stain.
entries.meaning_it: Tra due pari nessuno prevale: meglio accordarsi.
entries.meaning_en: Equals can't beat each other.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Quannu l'amuri voli trova locu.
entries.literal_it: Quando l'amore vuole trova posto.
entries.literal_en: When love wants, it finds a place.
entries.meaning_it: Chi vuole davvero trova il modo.
entries.meaning_en: Where there's a will there's a way.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Larga un ci veni e stritta un ci trasi.
entries.literal_it: Larga non gli viene e stretta non gli entra.
entries.literal_en: Too wide doesn't fit him, too tight won't go in.
entries.meaning_it: Si dice di chi non è mai contento.
entries.meaning_en: Said of someone never satisfied.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Unni cci chiovi cci sciddica.
entries.literal_it: Dove gli piove gli scivola.
entries.literal_en: Where it rains on him, it slides off.
entries.meaning_it: Si dice di chi non si preoccupa di nulla e cade sempre in piedi.
entries.meaning_en: Said of someone things just slide off.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Quandu si cunta è nenti.
entries.literal_it: Quando si racconta è niente.
entries.literal_en: When you can tell it, it's nothing.
entries.meaning_it: Finché sei vivo per raccontarlo, nessun guaio è troppo grave.
entries.meaning_en: If you live to tell it, it's nothing.
entries.usage_context: Consolation after a bad day or an incident.
entries.geographical_area: Catania (attributed as Catanese by the source)

entries.original: Tri pila avi u poccu.
variants: U porcu avi sulu tri pila.
entries.literal_it: Il porco ha solo tre peli.
entries.literal_en: The pig has only three bristles.
entries.meaning_it: Situazione o persona che non cambia mai; causa persa.
entries.meaning_en: A lost cause; someone who never changes.
entries.usage_context: Colleague who never changes habits; legacy code.
entries.geographical_area: Catania (attributed as Catanese by the source)
entries.notes: poccu = Catanese assimilated form of porcu.

entries.original: Essiri a vintitri uri e tri quarti.
entries.literal_it: Essere alle ventitré e tre quarti.
entries.literal_en: To be at 23:45.
entries.meaning_it: Essere agli sgoccioli (della vita, di una scadenza).
entries.meaning_en: To be at the eleventh hour.
entries.geographical_area: Catania (attributed as Catanese by the source)

entries.original: Tirari acqua cu lu panaru.
entries.literal_it: Tirare acqua con il paniere.
entries.literal_en: To draw water with a basket.
entries.meaning_it: Usare uno strumento inadatto, fatica inutile.
entries.meaning_en: Using the wrong tool; futile effort.
entries.usage_context: Wrong tool for the job (e.g. regex for HTML).
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: A lingua non avi ossa e rumpi ossa.
entries.literal_it: La lingua non ha ossa e rompe le ossa.
entries.literal_en: The tongue has no bones but breaks bones.
entries.meaning_it: Le chiacchiere fanno grandi danni.
entries.meaning_en: Words can do great harm.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Scacciari na mennula ca frunti.
entries.literal_it: Schiacciare una mandorla con la fronte.
entries.literal_en: To crack an almond with your forehead.
entries.meaning_it: Sottovalutare un grosso rischio.
entries.meaning_en: To underestimate a big risk.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: U malu tempu e u bon tempu non durunu tuttu u tempu.
entries.literal_it: Il brutto e il bel tempo non durano per sempre.
entries.literal_en: Bad weather and good weather don't last forever.
entries.meaning_it: Periodi buoni e cattivi si alternano.
entries.meaning_en: Good and bad times alternate.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Chistu è un muzzicuni di pulici.
entries.literal_it: Questo è un morso di pulce.
entries.literal_en: This is a flea bite.
entries.meaning_it: È un problema da poco.
entries.meaning_en: It's just a scratch.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Spassu di fora e triulu 'ncasa.
entries.literal_it: Spasso fuori e tribolo in casa.
entries.literal_en: Fun outside, trouble at home.
entries.meaning_it: Simpatico con gli altri, insopportabile in casa.
entries.meaning_en: Charming outside, a pain at home.
entries.usage_context: Colleague nice in public, nasty in private.
entries.geographical_area: pan-Sicilian (attested form; also current in Catania)

entries.original: Sperdiri a trunzu.
entries.literal_it: Finire a torsolo.
entries.literal_en: To end as a core (stump).
entries.meaning_it: Finire male.
entries.meaning_en: To end badly.
entries.geographical_area: Catania (Martoglio)

entries.original: Fici comu a chiddu.
entries.literal_it: Feci come quello.
entries.literal_en: I did like that one.
entries.meaning_it: Fare di necessità virtù.
entries.meaning_en: To make a virtue of necessity.
entries.geographical_area: Catania (Martoglio)
